$comment: Language-neutral conformance fixtures for the sprite-direct wire protocol. Source of truth: sprite-direct.el. Every per-language client's unit test suite must consume this file verbatim rather than hand-copying these cases, so a fixed protocol bug in one language's test data is caught in all four.

encode_decode.$comment: decoded (raw Lisp-printed text) <-> encoded (wire form after server-quote-arg-style escaping). Table: & -> &&, - -> &-, space -> &_, newline -> &n. All other bytes pass through unchanged.

sexp_print.$comment: Tagged-union sexp forms and their expected printed (Lisp reader syntax) output, BEFORE wire-protocol encoding is applied. Each 'form' node is {type: sym|str|int|float|list|quote, value: ...}, where list/quote values are themselves form nodes.

response_reassembly.$comment: Each case is the raw byte stream a server would send over the socket (joined with \n, EOF at end), and the expected parsed result after buffering to EOF, splitting on lines, and decoding -print/-print-nonl/-error payloads. The -emacs-pid preamble line must be tolerated and ignored, never treated as part of the result. A real Emacs server always builds replies with (pp v), which appends exactly one trailing newline before wire-encoding; exactly one trailing newline must be stripped from the final decoded/concatenated result (see the 'pp-style trailing newline' case).

cases.name: single print, no preamble stripped incorrectly
print-nonl continuation, no terminal marker, concatenated in line order
single print with a real Emacs pp-style trailing newline, stripped

expected.message: Symbol's function definition is void: foo

cases.name: preamble only, no print/error line at all -> treated as failed/empty
